name: Windows Update Issue
description: Diagnose failed, stalled, pending, or restart-required Windows updates with safe checks, bounded recovery, and explicit verification.

confirm_windows.question: Is this a Windows device that you can inspect under its update policy?
confirm_windows.help_text: Saving work first makes a possible Windows restart safer.

yes.label: Yes - I have saved my work and can inspect it

managed.label: A policy or administrator controls updates

unsupported_platform.title: Use Guidance for This Operating System
unsupported_platform.message: This workflow is designed for Windows. Choose platform-specific update guidance or correct the active device profile before continuing.

inspect_update_state.title: Inspect the Current Update State
inspect_update_state.instruction: Open Settings > Windows Update. Record the displayed status, any update name or identifier, any error code, and whether Windows says a restart is required. Do not install or restart yet.
inspect_update_state.help_text: The current Windows Update status determines the safest next step and preserves useful details if escalation is needed.

classify_update_state.question: What does Windows Update currently report?

failed.label: An update failed or shows an error

pending.label: An update is pending or in progress

managed.label: A policy, service, or organization message blocks updates

clarify_update_state.title: Review the Status One More Time
clarify_update_state.instruction: On the Windows Update page, select Check for updates once and wait for the displayed status to settle. Record the exact wording and any error code. Do not repeatedly select Check for updates.

clarified_update_state.question: After the single check, which state is visible?

record_failure_details.title: Record the Failed Update
record_failure_details.instruction: Record the update name, failure time, and error code shown in Windows Update or Update history. Keep those details for support. Do not delete update folders or reset Windows Update components.
record_failure_details.help_text: The exact update and error distinguish storage, policy, service, and servicing problems without making broad system changes.

classify_failure.question: What kind of blocker does Windows identify?

observe_update_progress.title: Observe One Update Interval
observe_update_progress.instruction: Keep the computer connected to power and the internet. Note the displayed percentage or status, wait ten minutes without repeatedly checking, then compare the status again.
observe_update_progress.help_text: A bounded observation distinguishes slow progress from a stalled update without interrupting Windows servicing.

progress_result.question: What happened during the observation interval?

inspect_storage.title: Inspect Available Storage
inspect_storage.instruction: Open Settings > System > Storage and review the Windows drive. Note any low-storage warning or message that the update needs more space. Do not delete files yet.
inspect_storage.help_text: Windows needs free storage for updates and temporary servicing files. This step observes capacity before any cleanup.

storage_result.question: Does Windows report low storage or that the update needs more space?

low_storage_handoff.title: Continue to Low Disk Space
low_storage_handoff.message: Low or uncertain storage can block Windows Update. Use the dedicated Low Disk Space workflow to verify capacity and review cleanup choices without deleting system folders or unfamiliar files.
low_storage_handoff.help_text: The dedicated workflow keeps cleanup bounded and leaves important-file decisions with the user.

restart_attempt_status.question: Has Windows already been restarted once for this update problem?
restart_attempt_status.help_text: One controlled restart is different from repeatedly restarting through the same failure.

restart_windows_safely.title: Complete One Controlled Restart
restart_windows_safely.instruction: Save all work. If this is a managed device, follow the organization's update policy. Use Start > Power > Restart once, keep the computer connected to power, and allow Windows to finish any update screen without forcing shutdown.
restart_windows_safely.help_text: A single controlled restart can complete a pending update. Repeated or forced restarts can interrupt servicing.

post_restart_state.question: After signing in, what does Windows Update report?

healthy.label: Up to date or the intended update completed

same.label: The same restart or pending state remains

error.label: The update failed or shows an error

managed.label: A policy or organization message is shown

verify_update_state.title: Verify the Update Result
verify_update_state.instruction: Return to Settings > Windows Update. Confirm whether the intended update completed or progress resumed, and check that Windows shows no blocking update error.
verify_update_state.help_text: A changed percentage alone is not final success; Windows must also show no blocking error.

verification_result.question: Is the intended update complete, or progressing with no blocking error?

complete.label: The update completed with no blocking error

progressing.label: Progress resumed and no blocking error is shown

monitor_update_completion.title: Update Progress Restored
monitor_update_completion.message: Windows Update is progressing without a blocking error. Keep the computer connected to power and the internet, allow the update to finish, and verify the final Windows Update status before considering the update complete.

verify_intended_update.question: Did the intended update complete, and does Windows show no blocking update error?

resolved_update.title: Windows Update Verified
resolved_update.message: The intended update completed and Windows reports no blocking update error. Keep normal update maintenance enabled and monitor for recurrence.

managed_or_service_support.title: Managed Update Support Required
managed_or_service_support.message: A policy, administrator, or service restriction is blocking Windows Update. Record the exact message and contact the device administrator or support team. Do not disable security controls or start, stop, or reconfigure unfamiliar services.

servicing_support.title: Windows Servicing Review Required
servicing_support.message: Windows reports a servicing, component-store, or system-file problem. Preserve the error code and contact a qualified technician. Diagnostic or repair tools such as DISM and SFC require an approved servicing plan and are not run automatically by this workflow.

persistent_failure_support.title: Persistent Update Failure Needs Support
persistent_failure_support.message: The supported first-line checks did not clear the update problem. Provide the update name, error code, update-history result, storage status, and restart result to support. Do not delete system folders, reset update components, or repeatedly restart the device.

uncertain_state_support.title: Update State Could Not Be Verified
uncertain_state_support.message: The current update state or result is not clear enough for a safe next action. Capture the Windows Update screen and any error code, then contact support rather than guessing or applying broad repairs.
